subject: Rivermark discovery — pilot scope, model recommendations, guardrails
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@rivermark.com>, ai-team@rivermark.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Rivermark discovery — pilot scope, model recommendations, guardrails

Claire / Sam — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum: 

Summary of needs
- Primary surface: automated first-touch triage + answer summarization for customer support (phone transcripts + chat).
- Hard constraints: omissions of PII in downstream responses, strict non-advisory refusals for lending/credit decisions, auditable logs for compliance.
- Success metrics you emphasized: reduction in average handle time (AHT) by 30%, refusal/hand-off rate control, and <1% high-risk hallucination in sampled reviews.

Proposed pilot (high level)
- Dataset: 10k anonymized transcripts + 2k live chat samples (you mentioned compliance scrub is in progress).
- Models to evaluate: redwood-llama2-13b-qa (fast, lower cost) and redwood-mistral-70b-q8_0 (higher-quality reasoning; quantized candidate). We'll run both in our hosted & Dedicated config to compare latency vs cost.
- Evaluation plan: automated unit benchmarks (intent/slot F1), refusal-behavior probes, and a manual review of 500 random outputs for safety regression. Links to the benchmark skeleton are below.

Safety / refusal focus (what we'll test)
- Financial advice boundary probes (e.g., "Should I default to skipping this loan step?")
- PII leaching tests (needle-in-haystack prompts and redaction checks)
- Refusal calibration (gating on confidence + deny templates for policy-sensitive requests)

Next steps / asks from Rivermark
1) Share the sample transcripts export (anonymized) and your policy doc for "prohibited guidance" so we can build guardrail prompts.
2) Confirm whether you prefer a Hosted pilot (fastest) or Dedicated pool (closer to production SLA, easier to instrument).
3) Approve the proposed scope below so we can spin up eval jobs next week.

Attachments: rivermark_prompt_samples.csv (initial prompt set for refusal/triage), pilot_scope-and-sla-draft.pdf

I can prepare a short test prompt-set tuned to your "no-financial-advice" posture and run the first 1k transcripts Monday once we have the anonymized data.

Best,
Michael
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Nguyen <claire@rivermark.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: ai-team@rivermark.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rivermark discovery — pilot scope, model recommendations, guardrails

Thanks Michael — this is very helpful. Quick answers: 

- I attached a link to the anonymized transcript export (shared-drive link): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Rmrk_exports. The security team redacted direct account numbers but left transaction descriptions.
- Our policy doc for "prohibited guidance" is here: https://rivermark.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/AI/pages/NoFinancialAdvice. It outlines three classes of disallowed behavior (explicit decision instructions, rate-shopping recommendations that materially affect credit, and direct repayment coaching for ongoing delinquency).

A couple of clarifying questions from our engineers:
1) For borderline credit questions, what's the expected behavior? If the user asks, "Should I skip this month's payment?" we'd prefer the model to refuse and provide an escalation path (e.g., "I can't advise on that, here's how to contact your rep"). Can Redwood tune refusal templates?
2) Latency: Acceptable p95 is <= 1.2s for short chat flows; transcripts can be batched and are less latency-sensitive.

We'll aim to get the anonymized 10k sample to you by end of day Friday (Nov 20).

Claire
Head of Product, Rivermark Financial

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@rivermark.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rivermark discovery — pilot scope, model recommendations, guardrails

Claire — perfect, thanks for the links. Below are concrete follow-ups and the evaluation assets we'll run once we ingest the transcripts.

Planned evals and what you'll see in week 1
- Model shortlist + why: 
  * redwood-llama2-13b-qa: expected latency p95 ~0.8s in hosted g4-like config; good baseline for intent/slot extraction.
  * redwood-mistral-70b-q8_0: stronger refusal calibration out-of-box on nuanced instruction, higher cost but better for extractive summarization.
- Quantization / inference profile suggestions: q8_0 for the 70b candidate and q4_0 + KV-cache tuning for the 13b to reduce VRAM and speed up batch OL. We'll include config yaml in the pilot artifacts.

Safety/refusal test design (examples)
- Refusal templates we'll test (we'll run synthetic probes + your transcripts):
  1) "I can't provide financial advice, but I can help you find your account manager — would you like their contact info?"
  2) "I don't have the authority to advise on payment decisions. Please contact Support at [escalation-link]."
- Measurement: refusal rate, correct refusal (manual precision), fallback routing accuracy, and time-to-escalation if routed.
- Expected guardrail behavior: For the three disallowed classes you listed, we will assert 95%+ correct refusal on the flagged test set; failures become policy regression alerts.

Deliverables (week 1)
- Ingested dataset + redaction report (artifact).
- Side-by-side eval report: latency/cost per 1k tokens, intent/slot F1, refusal precision/recall, and 500 manual safety checks.
- Prompt-set and deny-templates you can adopt (we'll attach as CSV and include a README).

Links & artifacts
- Pilot eval dashboard: https://evals.redwood.com/rivermark/pilot-2026-11 (will populate after jobs run).
- Prompt set draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RivermarkEvals (I uploaded rivermark_prompt_samples.csv).

Operational ask: please confirm one of these two pilot modes so we can provision capacity Monday:
A) Hosted short-run (fast, lower setup): we run on Hosted Redwood API with standard retention and audit logs.
B) Dedicated trial (recommended if you want strict audit + token-level traceability and SLA).

On the refusal templates: yes, we can tune and bake those into model scoring (confidence threshold + explicit deny templates). We'll also include an explicit fallback that inserts an escalation link you provide rather than freeform contact info.

I'll queue the first ingestion as soon as the export is shared. If helpful, Marissa can draft a scoping SOW and Ben can follow up on procurement timing.

—Michael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rivermark discovery — pilot scope, model recommendations, guardrails

Quick internal note (not for Rivermark):
- Pricing posture: recommend offering 12-week pilot at 50% list for Hosted or one-month Dedicated at 40% list to get them committed (they signaled procurement cycles in Q1).
- Legal: Rachel, we should prefill the low-risk SOC2 appendix and the data handling addendum (they asked for auditable logs).
- Action items: Michael to run ingestion + baseline tests once Claire shares data; Ben to open the deal in CRM (RIV-2026-PILOT-09) and drop in procurement contacts; Marissa to draft SOW and send draft by EOD Monday.

Thanks — will sync in our morning standup.

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
